NDT training in Montreal: how it works for Montreal employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT provides ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET for Montreal and Quebec employers, live online or onsite at your plant or shop, under ASNT Level III oversight. Atlantis has no Montreal campus. The training suits companies certifying staff under an SNT-TC-1A written practice, usually for US customers or US codes. It is not CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification, Canada's national scheme, and Atlantis does not claim CGSB recognition.

Greater Montreal is one of the most varied NDT markets in Canada. It has a large aerospace cluster, major hydroelectric and heavy-industry infrastructure, refining and petrochemical plants in the east end, a busy port, and a dense network of bridges, overpasses and transit structures. Each sector has its own certification expectations. Most Canadian-regulated work expects CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification issued by Natural Resources Canada's National NDT Certification Body, and the CWB Group is also authorized to certify NDT personnel. Aerospace suppliers often have to meet NAS 410 or EN 4179 on top of that, through their customer's specification. CGSB training has to come from an NRCan Recognized Training Organization. Atlantis does not claim that status and does not provide NAS 410 or EN 4179 training.

So who in Montreal benefits from SNT-TC-1A training? Quebec manufacturers and machine shops supplying US industrial customers (valves, pumps, castings, forgings, fabricated assemblies) whose purchase orders call for NDT personnel qualified to SNT-TC-1A. Also inspection companies and subsidiaries of US groups running a group-wide SNT-TC-1A written practice, and contractors sending crews to US plants, especially in the northeastern states. For these employers Atlantis supplies training, examinations and Level III oversight, and writes written practices that work next to CGSB-certified staff.

One Quebec detail to raise early is language. Quebec's Charter of the French Language shapes workplace documentation, and many Montreal employers expect procedures, examinations and training records to be available in French. Tell us your language requirements when you ask for a quote so we can confirm how the programme and its documents will be handled before anything is scheduled.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Montreal

All courses follow the SNT-TC-1A recommended body of knowledge. The written practice sets the formal training and experience hours. See the training requirements matrix for the recommended figures instead of relying on a number quoted here.

MethodLevelsWhat Montreal employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, IIIWeld inspection on fabricated and pressure components, forging and plate inspection, thickness surveys in east-end process plantsLevel I: employer entry rules. Level II: Level I plus logged experience
PAUT (phased array)II, IIIWeld inspection replacing RT in fabrication, corrosion mapping, inspection of forgings and heavy componentsUT Level II normally first
TOFDII, IIIFlaw sizing in heavy-section welds on pressure equipment and hydro componentsUT Level II normally first
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, IIICasting and weld radiography in foundries and fabrication shops, film and digital interpretationCNSC exposure device rules apply separately
MT (magnetic particle)I, II, IIISteel bridge and structural weld inspection, forgings, rail and heavy-equipment components, lifting gearEmployer entry rules
PT (liquid penetrant)I, II, IIIStainless and non-ferrous components, castings, machined partsEmployer entry rules
VT (visual testing)I, II, IIIWeld and fit-up inspection, structural condition surveys, in-service visual on pressure equipmentEmployer entry rules
ET (eddy current)I, II, IIISurface-crack detection on conductive parts, heat exchanger tubes, sorting and conductivity checks in metal manufacturingEmployer entry rules

UT for manufacturing and plant work. Montreal's industrial base puts a lot of UT into manufacturing: forgings, plate and castings inspected before shipment, and welds on fabricated assemblies. UT Level I builds thickness gauging and straight-beam skills. Level II adds angle-beam weld inspection, DAC and TCG, flaw characterisation, and evaluation against the governing standard, whether that's ASME Section VIII or the customer's own specification. In-service thickness surveys in the Montreal-East process area are covered too.

PAUT and TOFD. These advanced techniques are taught at Level II and III on top of UT Level II: focal laws, sectorial and linear scans, encoded scans, setup files and data review. Shops replacing RT with PAUT to free up floor space and cut radiation controls are a growing source of demand. TOFD is taught for sizing on heavy-section welds, including the large fabrications used in hydroelectric and heavy industry.

RT. Source and X-ray principles, image quality indicators, film and digital techniques, and interpretation of weld and casting discontinuities. Foundries and fabrication shops in the Montreal area often use fixed X-ray enclosures, so the course covers shop radiography as well as field techniques. Radiation certification is separate (see FAQ).

MT, PT and VT. The workhorse surface methods. MT supports structural steel, bridge work and heavy components. PT covers stainless, aluminium and other non-ferrous parts. VT underpins every weld and structural inspection. Courses cover technique selection, process controls and interpretation against acceptance criteria.

ET. Impedance-plane analysis, probe selection, reference standards, surface-crack detection and tube inspection, plus conductivity and material sorting applications used in metal manufacturing. Aerospace customers usually require NAS 410 or EN 4179 qualification, which Atlantis does not provide. Our ET course is SNT-TC-1A-based.

Level III. Live online ASNT Level III exam preparation for Quebec candidates.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Montreal, step by step

SNT-TC-1A certification is issued by the employer against its own written practice. The sequence is:

  1. Written practice. The employer writes and adopts a written practice setting out levels, training, experience, examinations, vision and certifying authority. In Quebec, consider the language of this document early. See written practice development.
  2. Formal training. Complete the required classroom hours for the method and level, delivered live online, onsite or both. The requirements matrix lists recommended hours.
  3. Experience. Log supervised experience in the method, in the hours required by the written practice, with sign-off.
  4. General examination. Written, on method theory.
  5. Specific examination. Written, on the employer's procedures, equipment and the codes or customer specifications that apply, for example a US customer's NDT specification for forgings.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on, on specimens with known flaws, administered and graded by a Level III or designee under the written practice.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, with near vision checked annually.
  8. Certification. The employer's certifying authority signs and records it.
  9. Recertification. At the interval the written practice sets. Changing employer means certifying again under the new written practice.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Montreal crews

Atlantis has no classroom in Montreal. Programmes run as:

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led virtual sessions on Eastern Time, with mock examinations and progress tracking. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility. An instructor runs practicals and examinations at your plant, shop or foundry on your own equipment and representative parts, which ties the training directly to your procedures and products. See corporate NDT training.
  • Blended. Online theory followed by an onsite block for practicals and examinations.

For manufacturers the timing constraint is usually production schedules and customer audits, not turnarounds. The best time to train is ahead of an audit or a new US contract, so certifications are in place before the first shipment. For east-end process plants, shutdown timing matters as usual. Tell us your deadline and your language needs, and cohort or onsite quotes come back within one business day. Request a Montreal training quote.

Where NDT technicians work in Montreal

  • Aerospace. Greater Montreal is one of the world's major aerospace clusters, with aircraft, engine, landing gear, simulation and component manufacturers along with a large supplier base and MRO. NDT is essential here, but it is usually qualified under NAS 410 or EN 4179 and customer specifications, which Atlantis does not train for.
  • Hydroelectric and heavy industry. Quebec runs on hydroelectric power. Turbines, runners, penstocks, gates and the large fabrications behind them need UT, PAUT, TOFD, MT and PT during manufacture and outages. Metal production and primary processing add further work.
  • Refining and petrochemicals. The Montreal-East industrial zone has refining, petrochemical and fuel terminal operations that need in-service inspection with UT, PAUT, RT, ET, MT and PT, plus turnaround surges.
  • Bridges, roads and transit. Montreal's island geography means many steel and concrete bridges, overpasses and elevated structures. Steel fabrication and in-service inspection use MT, UT and VT on welds and connections, typically to CSA W59 and CSA S6 (the Canadian Highway Bridge Design Code) under provincial and federal owners.
  • Rail and transit equipment. Rolling stock manufacturing and maintenance use UT and MT on axles, wheels, bogies and welded structures.
  • Port of Montreal. Cranes, terminals and marine structures need structural and lifting-equipment inspection.
  • General manufacturing. Foundries, forge shops, valve and pump makers, and fabrication shops, many of them exporting to the US.

Codes and regulators. Pressure equipment in Quebec is regulated by the Régie du bâtiment du Québec (RBQ) under the province's pressure-installation rules, with CSA B51 as the national baseline and ASME Section VIII and B31.3 as common design and construction codes. Structural welding follows CSA W59 and CSA W47.1 fabricator certification through the CWB, and bridges follow CSA S6. Industrial radiography is regulated federally by the CNSC. Workplace documentation follows the Charter of the French Language.

What Montreal employers typically ask for. CGSB certification for Canadian industrial and pressure-equipment work, NAS 410 or EN 4179 qualification for aerospace, CNSC certification for RT operators, and usually French-language ability. SNT-TC-1A certification appears mainly where the customer or parent company is American. For pay context, see the NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Montreal NDT companies

A Quebec manufacturer that wins a US order often finds an NDT clause in the purchase order requiring personnel qualified to SNT-TC-1A, and nothing in the company's current system covers it. Setting up a compliant programme quickly is what Atlantis does for these companies.

  • Written practice development. We write an SNT-TC-1A written practice for the methods and levels you use, taking into account any language requirements you need to meet. See written practice development.
  • Outsourced Level III. Procedures and technique sheets, examination preparation and grading, and customer audit support.
  • Purchase-order and specification review. We read the US customer's NDT clauses and map them to your procedures, acceptance criteria and reporting.
  • Programme coexistence. Where you also employ CGSB-certified staff, the written practice states clearly which scheme covers which customer and work.

Framework: SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Montreal company.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical NDT lets Atlantis trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five 3D environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Montreal manufacturing and fabrication trainees, the NDT lab and welding workshop scenes are the most relevant. Use it to rehearse technique and interpretation between onsite sessions. It is practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical examination on real specimens. For written exams, see UT Level 2 practice questions.

Your instructor

Programmes are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and written-practice work for Montreal employers.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Montreal

How do I get NDT certified in Montreal?

For most Canadian work, get CAN/CGSB-48.9712 certification through the NRCan NDT Certification Body, training with an NRCan Recognized Training Organization. If your employer certifies under an SNT-TC-1A written practice, the employer certifies you after training, experience, examinations and a vision test. Atlantis can deliver training and Level III examinations for that route.

Can I take NDT training online in Quebec?

Yes, for theory, which Atlantis runs live online. Practicals and the practical examination have to be hands-on and are delivered onsite at the employer's facility. See online NDT training.

Is the training available in French?

Tell us your language requirements when you ask for a quote. We will confirm what is possible for the course, examinations and documentation before you commit.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Montreal employers?

SNT-TC-1A certification is valid within the employer programme that issues it and is common where the customer or parent company is American. Most Canadian industrial work expects CGSB, and aerospace usually expects NAS 410 or EN 4179.

Does Atlantis training count toward CGSB?

No. NRCan requires CGSB training from its Recognized Training Organizations, and Atlantis does not claim that status.

Can Atlantis train aerospace NDT technicians to NAS 410?

No. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A only. NAS 410 and EN 4179 qualification needs a separate route.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

The written practice sets formal training and experience hours. The SNT-TC-1A recommendations are in the requirements matrix.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Quebec?

Gamma radiography falls under the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission. The employer holds a CNSC licence, and operators must be CNSC Certified Exposure Device Operators or trainees under direct supervision and continuous observation of one. X-ray equipment is also subject to provincial rules. Our RT course does not grant any radiation certification.

What does NDT training cost in Montreal?

Quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, delivery model, language needs, and whether Level III and written-practice services are included. We respond within one business day. Ask about onsite training for your Montreal team.

Can you train our shop onsite using our own parts?

Yes. Onsite practicals on your equipment and representative parts are the usual model for Montreal manufacturers.

Can I prepare for ASNT Level III from Montreal?

Yes. Level III preparation runs live online.

A US customer wants SNT-TC-1A. How quickly can we comply?

Start with a gap review. The timeline depends on your existing procedures and how much training and experience your staff already have. See written practice development.
